purpose.assets: Embedded HTML template and language icon assets used by renderers to produce the browser-facing output.
purpose.cmd/stacklit: Thin CLI executable entrypoint that delegates command handling to internal/cli.
purpose.internal/archexport: Transforms a Stacklit index into the architecture-export interchange document.
purpose.internal/cli: Cobra-style command layer for stacklit workflows including indexing, rendering, diffs, insights, derive output, and exit-code mapping.
purpose.internal/config: Project configuration loader and defaults for ignore rules, scan limits, and output paths.
purpose.internal/derive: Utilities that turn a schema index into compact injectable summaries and update target files with generated blocks.
purpose.internal/detect: Heuristics for detecting frameworks, environment variables, and repository conventions from files and imports.
purpose.internal/engine: Central orchestration layer that scans repositories, parses files, builds graphs, applies insights, and writes outputs.
purpose.internal/git: Git-derived activity and content identity helpers, including recent/hot file analysis and Merkle hashing.
purpose.internal/graph: Module dependency graph builder that groups parsed files, computes edges, entrypoints, isolated modules, and dependency rankings.
purpose.internal/hint: Derives actionable feature-placement guidance from indexed modules and entrypoints.
purpose.internal/insights: Load, merge, seed, apply, and write stacklit-insights.json purpose, hint, and architecture overlays.
purpose.internal/jsonfile: Shared JSON marshal and indented write helpers for stable formatted output files.
purpose.internal/monorepo: Repository workspace detector for monorepo tools and workspace layouts.
purpose.internal/parser: Language-aware source parsers that extract imports, exports, type definitions, line counts, and entrypoint flags.
purpose.internal/purpose: Supplies mechanical fallback module-purpose text when curated insight is unavailable.
purpose.internal/renderer: JSON, Markdown, Mermaid, and HTML output generation from the canonical schema index.
purpose.internal/schema: Canonical data model for project indexes, module metadata, dependencies, git activity, hints, and multi-repo summaries.
purpose.internal/summary: AI-assisted summary command integration that generates insights files from schema indexes.
purpose.internal/walker: Filesystem traversal with ignore handling to produce the source file list for indexing.
purpose.root: Shell installer and convenience indexing scripts outside the Go application packages.

hints.add_feature: For new CLI-visible behavior, start in internal/cli, delegate orchestration to internal/engine, add schema fields in internal/schema only when the output contract changes, and update renderer/insights handling for any new index data.

architecture.ai_summary:
Stacklit is a filesystem-to-index CLI; README.md explains this fork's replacement of MCP tools with plain commands. In the observed generate-json path, Cobra passes options to engine.Run, which resolves configuration, detects workspaces, walks eligible sources, parses files, builds the dependency graph, adds Git and framework metadata, computes a source fingerprint, applies insights, and writes JSON. Query, derive, visualization, and architecture-export commands consume that persisted snapshot. This separates expensive source discovery from repeated navigation; refreshing semantic insights requires another generate-json before index readers see them (README.md, internal/engine/engine.go).

Parsing produces FileInfo records, keeping language extraction separate from directory grouping and import resolution. Go uses its standard syntax-tree parser; supported other languages use per-call Tree-sitter state, with generic metadata fallback. The worker pool restores input order before graph assembly and collects per-file errors without aborting the scan. Configuration and CLI validation reject effective worker counts below one before scanning; CLI overrides configured values, and the default remains one. Graph assembly stays sequential, excludes fixture/test directories, and index assembly filters dependency references to retained modules after capping. These are observed enforcement points in internal/parser/parser.go, internal/graph/graph.go, and internal/engine/engine.go. Changing extraction alone can remain local when FileInfo semantics hold; changing module identity or output fields requires coordinated graph, schema, enrichment, and consumer changes.

The generated index is deliberately selective rather than a complete program model. Source eligibility, depth limits, export truncation, and heuristic import matching determine what survives. Generation tolerates missing Git information and individual parse failures; malformed insights and output failures abort. RunMulti scans repositories sequentially, writes their outputs, and aggregates successful indexes; worker-configuration errors abort, while other scan failures warn and skip. Configured generated outputs are excluded from scans to prevent feedback. Diff compares a Merkle fingerprint, a hash tree over selected paths and contents, with exit codes 0/current, 1/changed, and 2/failure; it does not establish semantic insight freshness (internal/cli/diff.go). JSON rendering preserves timestamps for semantically unchanged output and skips identical writes.

Semantic enrichment has its own lifecycle: init-insights seeds missing knowledge, ai-summary invokes one local agent, and Stacklit merges and writes the returned insights. Exact module-purpose keys override basename keys when applied. Merge preserves customized purposes and test commands while replacing generated defaults and accepting a new summary. Fresh drafting before reconciliation is a prompt requirement, not filesystem isolation. The direct Anthropic helper is separate from the CLI path (internal/cli/insights.go, internal/insights/insights.go, internal/summary/cli.go). Consult USAGE.md for invocation and refresh details.

Implementations must respect Go 1.25.0 in go.mod and retain copyright and permission notices under LICENSE's MIT terms. README.md defines the fork's CLI-only product surface; GUARDRAILS.md adds no concrete product constraints. specs/map-reduce.md requires scheduling changes to preserve schema and graph semantics; its draft plans are historical, while specs/benchmarks/map-reduce/benchmark-report.md supplies dated latency/memory evidence. Worker limits bound active parses, not total scan memory: engine retains source contents later. Consult purpose, hints, and stacklit derive next for navigation; this summary adds runtime sequencing, failure boundaries, and the contracts that must evolve together.
